message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time Zone) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
However, because both regions observe daylight‑saving time (DST), the offset can shift:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Offset |
|--------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Standard time (winter) | PST (UTC−8) | CET (UTC+1) | –9 h |
| Daylight‑time overlap (spring/fall) | PDT (UTC−7) | CEST (UTC+2) | –9 h |
| When only one region is on DST | e.g., Los Angeles on PDT (UTC−7) while Berlin still on CET (UTC+1) | –8 h |
| When only Berlin is on DST | e.g., Los Angeles on PST (UTC−8) while Berlin on CEST (UTC+2) | –10 h |

So, at most times of the year the difference is 9 hours, but it can temporarily become 8 or 10 hours during the weeks when the two regions switch DST at different dates.
